JDK Proxy implements the exact borrowed public Hikari MXBean interface using its defining class loader and an allowlisted fake getter handler. This preserves SDK interface identity, creates no pool/config/JMX connection and exposes no credential/control getter. Dependency hashes and all original cases are frozen; no context-classloader fallback or reflective access.

Reservation is a memory-accounting token, not an FD/stream or externally acquired resource. Original case explicitly checks close/repeated close, ownership transfer and retained bytes; retain deliberately prevents rollback and one callback performs retain/close. Replacing this oracle with implicit TWR rollback changes the tested lifetime. Every fixture is local; no physical file or capacity scan exists.

The test deliberately holds each publicly visible capacity/reservation monitor while a separately owned worker completes reserve/retain/close with5-second deadline. Production uses its own ReentrantLock. This is a negative caller-monitor independence oracle, not production synchronization; replacing the held monitor removes that oracle.
